image_description: A close-up, high-resolution shot of an African crocodile's head and upper jaw. The mouth is slightly open, revealing interlocking conical teeth. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing rough, bony scutes on the dorsal surface and smoother scales near the jawline. The eye is visible with a vertical slit pupil. The background is blurred, focusing entirely on the reptile's head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers to a distinct V-shape, consistent with Crocodylus niloticus morphology, distinguishing it from the U-shaped snout of alligators.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Teeth are clearly visible, conical, and appear to interlock correctly. The fourth lower tooth fits into the upper jaw notch as expected.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Eye is positioned on top of the skull. Vertical slit pupil is clearly visible. Nictitating membrane structure is plausible though not fully deployed.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The extreme close-up framing cuts off the very tip of the snout where nostrils would be located; they are outside the field of view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the head and neck region are visible; the full body elongation cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal skin behind the eye shows characteristic rough, raised osteoderms/scutes with irregular but natural-looking arrangement.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Coloration is greyish-brown with significant textural variation consistent with real crocodile skin.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The inner jaw/lower neck area shows smoother, lighter-colored scaling compared to the dorsal armor, consistent with ventral/soft tissue scales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Limbs are completely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Tail is not visible in this head-shot crop.

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification of species-specific features (snout shape, tooth arrangement, scale texture) against ImageNet classes.
To detect subtle AI artifacts in complex textures like overlapping scales and translucent teeth edges.
To ensure no melting or fusion between the teeth, gums, and eye structures, which are common failure points in AI generation.

focus_areas: Eye anatomical correctness (pupil shape, eyelid structure)
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the hard scutes and the softer skin around the jaw. AI often blurs this boundary. Verify that the teeth do not 'melt' into the gum line and that the eye reflection is physically consistent with the lighting direction.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
